q: A deviation statement prepared at the final bill stage of a works contract serves primarily to:

options.A: Tabulate the rates quoted by all the tenderers item-wise for comparison
options.B: Record the hindrances encountered during the execution of the work
options.C: Compare, item-wise, the quantities provided in the agreement with the quantities actually executed, so that the excesses and shortages on each item are brought out
options.D: Summarise the cost of the work sub-head-wise for the sanction of its estimate

e: A deviation statement, prepared with the final bill under the Engineering Code, compares item-wise the quantities in the agreement with those actually executed, bringing out excesses and shortages on each item so that deviations needing sanction are identified.

q: Every running or final bill of a works contractor is accompanied by a statement of the recoveries due from him, such as the cost of departmental materials, hire charges of tools and plant and security deposit. The purpose of this statement is to ensure that:

options.A: The contractor's earnest money is refunded along with the first bill itself
options.B: The gross value of the work done is enhanced by the amount of the recoveries
options.C: The recoveries are postponed until the defect liability period of the work expires
options.D: All the amounts due to the Railways are deducted from the gross amount of the bill, so that only the net amount payable is passed for payment

e: Every running or final bill carries a statement of recoveries - cost of departmental materials, hire of tools and plant, security deposit and other dues - so that all amounts due to the Railways are deducted from the gross bill value and only the net amount is passed for payment.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Appropriation audit of works expenditure is directed to seeing that the expenditure was incurred with due sanction, that funds were allotted for it, and that it was incurred for the purpose for which the grant was made.
2. Appropriation audit dispenses with the internal check of works bills exercised by the Accounts office before payment.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Appropriation audit verifies that works expenditure was duly sanctioned, funds were allotted and the grant was used for its intended purpose. It is an audit function and does not dispense with the Accounts office internal check of bills before payment, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: The proposals of a Zonal Railway for new works to be included in the annual Works Programme are processed and scrutinised through the web-based system known as:

options.A: The Indian Railways e-Procurement System used for inviting tenders
options.B: The Indian Railways Projects Sanctions and Management system
options.C: The portal used by contractors for recording electronic measurements
options.D: The Government e-Marketplace used for procuring common services

e: Works Programme proposals of Zonal Railways are processed and scrutinised through IRPSM - Indian Railways Projects Sanctions and Management - the web-based system for project sanctions. IREPS is for tenders, GeM for common procurement, so those do not fit.

q: Temporary departmental works which are necessary only for the execution of a sanctioned work, such as a site approach, a temporary water supply arrangement or a site office shed of the department, and which are dismantled when the work is finished, are dealt with in accounts by:

options.A: Charging their cost to the sanctioned work itself, as a part of the cost of executing that work
options.B: Treating them as permanent assets of the division in every case
options.C: Recovering their cost from the contractor executing the work in all cases
options.D: Booking their cost permanently under a suspense head

e: Temporary departmental works needed only to execute a sanctioned work, such as a site approach, temporary water supply or site shed, are ancillary to that work and dismantled on completion, so their cost is charged to the sanctioned work itself as part of its execution cost.

q: An asset created under a work is permanently dismantled and removed from use, and the materials released from it are disposed of. In the asset records of the Railways, the correct treatment is that:

options.A: The recorded cost of the asset continues to stand in the Block Account indefinitely
options.B: The asset is transferred to the Contractor's Ledger for adjustment
options.C: The cost of the dismantled asset is debited afresh to the renewal work
options.D: The recorded cost of the asset is removed from the Block Account and the asset register with the sanction of the competent authority, so that the capital-at-charge does not continue to include an asset which no longer exists

e: When an asset is permanently dismantled, its recorded cost must be removed from the Block Account and asset register with competent sanction; otherwise capital-at-charge would continue to include a non-existent asset. Sale proceeds and released materials are accounted for separately.

q: The outstanding items under Miscellaneous Works Advances are watched by agreement between the executive and the Accounts office. This agreement is carried out by ensuring that:

options.A: The balances are agreed only with the Contractor's Ledger of the division
options.B: The schedule of outstanding items prepared by the executive agrees with the balances appearing in the accounts books, differences being investigated and set right
options.C: The outstanding items are compared with the allotment of the work in the Pink Book
options.D: The items are verified only against the tender documents of the works concerned

e: Miscellaneous Works Advances outstandings are agreed between executive and Accounts by matching the executive schedule of outstanding items with the balances in the accounts books, with differences investigated and set right, as required for suspense and advance heads under the Accounts Code.

q: A contractor's bill, after it has been subjected to internal check in the Accounts office and found in order, is passed for payment by endorsing on it a:

options.A: Completion certificate for the work
options.B: Sanction of the competent authority to the estimate
options.C: Pay order, on the basis of which payment is arranged to the contractor
options.D: Letter of Acceptance of the tender for the work

e: After internal check finds a contractor bill in order, Accounts endorses a pay order on it, and payment is arranged on the authority of that pay order. A completion certificate, estimate sanction or Letter of Acceptance is a separate document, not the payment authority.

q: The expenditure incurred on testing, trial runs and commissioning of a newly created asset, up to the stage at which the asset is ready to be brought into regular use, is treated in accounts as:

options.A: A part of the capital cost of the asset, being expenditure directly attributable to bringing the asset into use
options.B: Ordinary repairs and maintenance expenditure of the year
options.C: An advance recoverable from the agency which carried out the testing
options.D: A charge on the earnings of the first year of working of the asset alone

e: Testing, trial runs and commissioning expenditure incurred up to the stage the asset is ready for regular use is directly attributable to bringing the asset into use, so it forms part of the capital cost of the asset, not ordinary repairs of the year.

q: Amounts received from contractors and tenderers by way of earnest money and security deposit, which are held by the Railways until they are refunded, adjusted or forfeited, are watched in the Accounts office through:

options.A: The Works Register maintained by the executive office
options.B: The deposits accounts and registers, in which each deposit received is recorded so that its refund, adjustment or forfeiture is properly accounted for
options.C: The Revenue Allocation Register maintained for works expenditure
options.D: The comparative statements of the tenders received for works

e: Earnest money and security deposits received from contractors and tenderers are held in deposit accounts and registers, where each deposit is recorded and watched until it is refunded, adjusted or forfeited, ensuring no deposit escapes accountal.

q: Railway land is demarcated on the ground, and protected against encroachment, by providing and maintaining:

options.A: Catch-water drains along the boundary of the land
options.B: Fouling marks at the converging lines adjoining the land
options.C: Gradient posts along the track passing through the land
options.D: Boundary stones or pillars along the limits of the land, which are verified during periodical inspections of the land

e: Railway land is demarcated and protected by boundary stones or pillars provided and maintained along its limits, as per the Engineering Code provisions on land management; they are verified during periodical land inspections to detect encroachment.

q: Finance has accorded its concurrence to a proposal for a work as put up to it. Thereafter, the executive materially changes the scope and cost of the proposal. The correct course is that:

options.A: The original concurrence automatically covers the changed proposal also
options.B: The changed proposal requires only the sanction of the executive authority, concurrence being a one-time formality
options.C: The proposal, as materially changed, must be referred to Finance again for fresh concurrence before it is sanctioned
options.D: The change can be regularised in the completion report of the work

e: Finance concurrence is given to a proposal as put up; if the executive thereafter materially changes its scope or cost, the changed proposal must go back to Finance for fresh concurrence before sanction, since the original concurrence does not cover the new proposal.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The financial powers given in the Schedule of Powers are exercisable subject to the conditions laid down therein, including the concurrence of Finance where such concurrence is prescribed.
2. The powers given in the Schedule of Powers can be exercised even where no funds have been allotted for the expenditure, the allotment being a separate matter which does not affect the sanction.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Powers in the Schedule of Powers are exercisable only subject to the conditions in it, including Finance concurrence where prescribed, and also require availability of funds. A sanction without allotted funds is not valid, so only statement 1 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A change in the scope or character of a sanctioned work, such as a change in the standard of construction adopted for it, can amount to a material modification even where the resulting increase in its cost is comparatively small.
2. Every increase in the cost of a work, from whatever cause, is by itself a material modification of the work, the scope of the work being irrelevant.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Material modification turns on change in scope or character, such as a change in the standard of construction, and can arise even for a small cost increase. A mere cost increase from other causes is not by itself a material modification, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: A revised estimate of a work is ordinarily accompanied by a comparative statement. The purpose of this statement is to:

options.A: Compare the rates quoted by the tenderers for the work with the schedule rates
options.B: Show, item-wise or sub-head-wise, the cost as originally sanctioned against the cost as now estimated, with the reasons for the increase or decrease under each head
options.C: Compare the cost of the work with the earnings expected from it in the first year
options.D: Record the measurements of the work executed up to the date of the revised estimate

e: A revised estimate is supported by a comparative statement showing, item-wise or sub-head-wise, the originally sanctioned cost against the now estimated cost with reasons for each increase or decrease, enabling the sanctioning authority to judge the revision.

q: Before the Notice Inviting Tender for a work is issued, Finance vetting of the schedule of quantities included in the tender documents is directed, among other things, to seeing that:

options.A: The contractor who will execute the work is identified in advance
options.B: The lowest rate acceptable for the work is fixed beforehand
options.C: The earnest money of every tenderer is received in advance
options.D: The items and quantities put to tender correspond to the scope of the sanctioned estimate, so that the tender does not cover work beyond the sanction accorded

e: Finance vetting of the schedule of quantities before the Notice Inviting Tender is issued ensures the items and quantities tendered correspond to the scope of the sanctioned estimate, so tendering does not cover work beyond the sanction accorded.

q: For determining the quantities of earthwork executed on a work, the levels of the ground are recorded before the earthwork is started and again after its completion. The levels recorded before the start of the work are required to be:

options.A: Recorded jointly and signed by the representative of the Engineer and the contractor, so that the original ground levels, on which the quantities will be computed, are agreed and not in dispute later
options.B: Recorded by the contractor alone in his own level book
options.C: Taken from the longitudinal section prepared at the survey stage of the line
options.D: Recorded only after the first running bill of the contractor has been paid

e: Earthwork quantities are computed from levels taken before and after execution, so the original ground levels must be recorded jointly and signed by the Engineer representative and the contractor, making the basis of computation agreed and undisputed later.

q: The sanction accorded to the estimate of a survey for a proposed new line has the effect that:

options.A: The new line itself stands sanctioned for construction
options.B: Tenders for the construction of the line can be invited at once
options.C: Only the survey is authorised to be carried out; the project itself requires separate sanction after the survey report has been examined
options.D: Funds for the construction of the line stand allotted for the year

e: Sanction to a survey estimate authorises only the survey itself. The project requires separate sanction after the survey report is examined; neither construction, tendering nor allotment of construction funds follows from survey sanction.

q: The cost of a work, as worked out from the tender proposed to be accepted, exceeds the sanctioned estimate of the work beyond the latitude permitted in such cases. In this position, the work:

options.A: Can be awarded at once, the excess being adjusted against the contingencies of other works
options.B: Cannot properly be awarded until a revised estimate covering the total cost is sanctioned by the competent authority
options.C: Can be awarded after obtaining only the verbal approval of the Engineer-in-charge
options.D: Must be awarded at the estimate rates by reducing the quantities in the agreement

e: Where the cost as per the tender proposed for acceptance exceeds the sanctioned estimate beyond the permitted latitude, the work cannot properly be awarded until a revised estimate covering the total cost is sanctioned by the competent authority.

q: A work is executed departmentally by the Railways with their own labour and materials, instead of through a contractor. The estimate and the accounts of such a work are framed on the basis that:

options.A: A contractor's profit element is added to the cost of the work as in a tendered work
options.B: Only the cost of materials is charged to the work, the labour being borne by the establishment grant in all cases
options.C: The work is executed without any sanctioned estimate, departmental execution requiring none
options.D: The cost charged to the work comprises the materials, labour, tools and plant and supervision actually employed on it, there being no element of a contractor's profit

e: In departmental execution the work is charged with materials, labour, tools and plant and supervision actually employed on it. No contractor profit element arises, since no contractor is engaged, though a sanctioned estimate is still required.

q: In the estimate of a renewal or replacement work, credit is taken for the materials released from the existing asset. The amount of this credit is worked out:

options.A: At the value assessed for the released materials, in accordance with the assessment made for the work
options.B: At the original cost at which the materials were first purchased for the asset
options.C: At the highest market price prevailing for new materials of the same description
options.D: At a uniform fixed amount prescribed for all renewal works

e: In a renewal or replacement estimate, credit for released materials is taken at the value assessed for them for that work, not at original purchase cost or at the market price of new materials, and the net cost is sanctioned accordingly.

q: The rates in the schedule of rates for items of work are framed with reference to materials being available within a normal distance of the site. Where the materials for a work have to be carried from a considerably greater distance, the estimate provides for this by:

options.A: Increasing the provision for contingencies of the work
options.B: Making a separate provision for the extra lead involved in bringing the materials to the site, in addition to the normal rate for the item
options.C: Charging the extra carriage to the contractor's security deposit
options.D: Omitting the carriage of materials from the estimate altogether

e: Schedule rates assume materials available within a normal lead; where materials must be carried from a considerably greater distance, the estimate makes a separate provision for the extra lead over and above the normal item rate.

q: Limited tenders for a work are invited by sending the tender documents to:

options.A: All the contractors who apply for them, whether enlisted or not
options.B: The contractor who executed the previous work in the section alone
options.C: Enlisted contractors of the class corresponding to the value of the tendered work, in accordance with the tender procedure
options.D: Government departments executing works on a deposit basis

e: Limited tenders are invited only from enlisted contractors of the class corresponding to the value of the tendered work, following the tender procedure in the Engineering Code and GCC; they are not open to all applicants or to a single past contractor.

q: The quantities shown in the schedule of quantities (Bill of Quantities) of an item-rate works tender are to be treated as:

options.A: Guaranteed quantities, for which the Railways must pay whether executed or not
options.B: Quantities which the contractor must execute in full even if the work requires less
options.C: Quantities which cannot be varied under any circumstances during execution
options.D: Approximate quantities given for the guidance of the tenderers, payment being made for the quantities actually executed and measured

e: Quantities in the Bill of Quantities of an item-rate tender are approximate, given for tenderers guidance. Payment is made for quantities actually executed and measured, and quantities may vary subject to the deviation provisions of the contract.

q: A member of a Tender Committee is unable to agree with the recommendation proposed to be made by the Committee on a tender. The correct course for such a member is to:

options.A: Record his dissent, with the reasons for it, in the proceedings of the Tender Committee
options.B: Refuse to attend all future meetings of the Committee
options.C: Communicate his views separately to the lowest tenderer
options.D: Accept the tender himself in place of the accepting authority

e: A Tender Committee member who cannot agree with the proposed recommendation must record his dissent with reasons in the committee proceedings, so the accepting authority decides with full knowledge of the differing view.

q: A works contractor appoints an authorised representative to attend to the work at the site. Instructions regarding the work given by the Engineer to this representative:

options.A: Bind the contractor only if they are separately repeated to the contractor at his head office
options.B: Are treated as instructions given to the contractor himself, the representative being authorised by the contractor to receive them on his behalf
options.C: Are of no effect, instructions being valid only when given to the Engineer by the contractor
options.D: Require the approval of the Tender Committee before the contractor acts on them

e: Instructions given by the Engineer to the contractor authorised representative at site are treated as instructions to the contractor himself, the representative being authorised to receive them on his behalf under the GCC.

q: Where a bid for a work is submitted by a company or a joint venture, the bid is required to be signed by:

options.A: Any employee of the company who is present at the time of submission
options.B: The Engineer-in-charge of the work on behalf of the bidder
options.C: A person duly authorised by the bidder to sign and submit the bid on its behalf, the authorisation being furnished as required by the tender documents
options.D: All the shareholders or members of the bidder in every case

e: A bid by a company or joint venture must be signed by a person duly authorised by the bidder to sign and submit it, with the authorisation furnished as required by the tender documents; an unauthorised employee signature is not valid.

q: Payments due to a works contractor under a passed bill are arranged by the Railways:

options.A: Through the contractor's bank account by electronic transfer, and not by cash payment to the contractor
options.B: In cash at the site of the work by the Engineer-in-charge
options.C: By adjustment against the earnest money of other tenderers
options.D: Only after the expiry of the defect liability period of the work

e: Payments due to a works contractor under a passed bill are made through his bank account by electronic transfer, not in cash at site, ensuring a traceable and secure payment as per current Railway payment instructions.

q: Under a works contract, the defaults and acts of the persons employed by the contractor on the work are dealt with on the principle that:

options.A: The Railways must proceed directly against each such person, the contractor having no responsibility for them
options.B: The sub-contractor alone is answerable to the Railways for the portion executed by him
options.C: The workmen engaged on the work become answerable to the Railways as its own staff
options.D: The contractor remains answerable to the Railways for the acts and defaults of his agents, sub-contractors and workmen engaged on the work, as if they were his own acts and defaults

e: Under the GCC the contractor remains answerable to the Railways for the acts and defaults of his agents, sub-contractors and workmen on the work, as if they were his own acts and defaults; the Railways need not proceed against each person separately.

q: The progress of a work falls behind the approved programme entirely on account of the contractor's failure to mobilise adequate resources. The Engineer requires him to speed up the work by deploying additional resources. The cost of such speeding up:

options.A: Is payable by the Railways as an extra item of work
options.B: Is to be borne by the contractor, the speeding up being required only to make good the delay caused by his own default and to complete the work by the stipulated date
options.C: Is shared equally between the Railways and the contractor in all cases
options.D: Is recovered from the tenderers who did not take up the work

e: Speeding up ordered only because the contractor fell behind through his own failure to mobilise resources is at the contractor cost; the Railways pay nothing extra for acceleration needed merely to meet the stipulated completion date.

q: The Engineer fixes the rate for an extra item of work in accordance with the contract, but the contractor disputes the rate so fixed. Pending the settlement of this dispute, the contractor:

options.A: May stop the whole work until the rate is settled to his satisfaction
options.B: May refuse to execute the extra item in all cases
options.C: Is required to carry on with the work, including the extra item, at the rate fixed, his remedy for the disputed rate lying through the claims and dispute-resolution provisions of the contract
options.D: Becomes entitled to payment at the rate claimed by him until the dispute is decided

e: Where the Engineer fixes a rate for an extra item and the contractor disputes it, the GCC requires the contractor to carry on the work, including the extra item, at the rate fixed, pursuing his remedy through the claims and dispute resolution provisions.

q: In evaluating the financial bids for a work, a discount offered by a tenderer which is conditional, for example on his being awarded another work also, is dealt with as follows:

options.A: It is not taken into account in the evaluation, unless the tender conditions expressly permit such conditional discounts to be considered
options.B: It is applied in full in favour of the tenderer in every case
options.C: It is converted into an unconditional discount by the Tender Committee
options.D: It entitles the tenderer to be treated as the lowest tenderer automatically

e: A conditional discount, such as one linked to award of another work, is not taken into account in bid evaluation unless the tender conditions expressly permit considering such discounts, since evaluation must be on the bids as invited.

q: The 'Instructions to Tenderers' forming part of the tender documents of a work lay down:

options.A: Only the technical specifications of the items of work
options.B: The measurements of the work after it is executed
options.C: The departmental charges leviable on deposit works
options.D: The manner of preparing and submitting the tender, the documents to accompany it and the procedure for its opening and evaluation, by which the tenderers are bound

e: The Instructions to Tenderers in the tender documents lay down how the tender is to be prepared and submitted, the documents to accompany it and the procedure for opening and evaluation, and tenderers are bound by them.

q: Departmental materials issued to a contractor for incorporation in a work are issued against material issue notes. These notes serve as the basis for:

options.A: Fixing the rates payable to the contractor for the items of the work
options.B: Effecting recovery of the value of the materials from the contractor's bills, the issue being acknowledged by the contractor or his representative
options.C: Preparing the comparative statement of the tenders for the work
options.D: Releasing the performance guarantee furnished by the contractor

e: Departmental materials issued to a contractor against material issue notes, acknowledged by him or his representative, form the basis for recovering the value of the materials from his bills, the notes evidencing the quantity and value issued.

q: A deposit work is executed by the Railways for an outside body. As regards the selection of the agency to execute the work:

options.A: The body for which the work is executed selects the contractor itself
options.B: The work is allotted without tenders at the rates demanded by the body
options.C: The Railways follow their own tender and contract procedure for the work, the body having no role in the selection of the contractor
options.D: The contractor is nominated jointly by the body and the tenderers of the division

e: Even for a deposit work, the Railways follow their own tender and contract procedure to select the executing agency; the outside body for which the work is done has no role in selecting the contractor.

q: Under an Annual Maintenance Contract for equipment, the contract provides a stipulated time within which the contracting agency must attend to a breakdown call. Where the agency repeatedly fails to attend within that time, the failure is dealt with by:

options.A: Effecting the deduction or penalty provided in the contract for such delayed or deficient service
options.B: Paying the agency an additional amount for attending the calls late
options.C: Extending the currency of the contract automatically as compensation
options.D: Recording the measurements of the delay in the Measurement Book as an item of work

e: Under an Annual Maintenance Contract, repeated failure to attend a breakdown within the stipulated time is dealt with by the deduction or penalty provided in the contract for delayed or deficient service, not by extra payment or automatic extension.

q: Samples of the materials proposed to be used on a work are got approved by the Engineer before the materials are used. The approved samples are retained at the site office in order to:

options.A: Be sold to the contractor after the work is completed
options.B: Be exhibited to the tenderers of the next work of the division
options.C: Fix the earnest money payable by the contractor for the work
options.D: Serve as the standard with which the materials actually brought to the site and used on the work can be compared during execution

e: Approved samples of materials are retained at the site office as the standard of quality and finish against which materials actually brought to site and used on the work are compared during execution.

q: The results of the tests carried out at the site on materials and on the work, such as the cube tests of concrete, are recorded as the work proceeds in a:

options.A: Hindrance Register maintained for the contract
options.B: Test register maintained at the site, which forms the record of the quality checks exercised on the work
options.C: Contractor's Ledger maintained in the Accounts office
options.D: Register of Sanctions maintained in the Accounts office

e: Site test results, such as concrete cube tests, are recorded progressively in a test register maintained at site, which forms the record of quality checks exercised on materials and the work.

q: Decisions taken in a periodical progress-review meeting for a work are recorded in the minutes of the meeting. Where a change in the work is discussed in such a meeting, the change can be executed by the contractor only when:

options.A: It has been noted in the minutes of the meeting, that by itself being sufficient authority
options.B: The contractor records it in his own site diary
options.C: It is ordered by the Engineer in writing as a variation or instruction under the contract, the minutes by themselves not being an order for a variation
options.D: The Accounts office has been informed of the discussion in the meeting

e: Minutes of a progress review meeting are only a record of discussion, not a variation order. A change discussed there can be executed only when the Engineer orders it in writing as a variation or instruction under the contract.

q: For the internal check of a contractor's bills, the Accounts office relies, besides the measurements, on the conditions and rates of the work as contained in:

options.A: A copy of the contract agreement of the work, which is furnished to the Accounts office and against which the bills are checked
options.B: The personal diary of the Engineer-in-charge of the work
options.C: The attendance register of the labour engaged by the contractor
options.D: The justification note prepared for the Works Programme proposal

e: For internal check of contractor bills, Accounts relies on a copy of the contract agreement furnished to it, checking the bills against its conditions, rates and quantities, besides the recorded measurements.

q: A theodolite, used in the survey of a proposed railway work, is an instrument which is used for measuring:

options.A: The distance between two points along the alignment directly
options.B: Horizontal and vertical angles with precision
options.C: The depth of the foundation pits of a structure
options.D: The bearing capacity of the soil at the site

e: A theodolite is a precision surveying instrument used for measuring horizontal and vertical angles. Distances, foundation depths and soil bearing capacity are determined by other means.

q: 'Centering' provided in the construction of an arch or a similar structure is:

options.A: The permanent masonry ring of the arch itself
options.B: The wall built at the end of the arch to retain the approach filling
options.C: The reinforcement placed in the concrete of the arch ring
options.D: The temporary framework or support on which the arch is built, which is removed after the arch masonry or concrete has set and gained strength

e: Centering is the temporary framework or support on which an arch is built; it is removed after the arch masonry or concrete has set and gained sufficient strength to be self-supporting.

q: The 'keystone' of a masonry arch is:

options.A: The stone laid at the springing of the arch, from which the arch ring starts
options.B: The filling provided over the arch between its extrados and the road or track above
options.C: The central wedge-shaped stone at the crown of the arch, which locks the other stones of the ring in position
options.D: The block provided under the bearing of the girder resting on the arch

e: The keystone is the central wedge-shaped stone at the crown of a masonry arch; once placed, it locks all the other stones of the arch ring in position. The stone at the springing is the springer, not the keystone.

q: The 'jamb' of a door or a window opening in a wall is:

options.A: The vertical side of the opening, to which the frame of the door or window is fixed
options.B: The horizontal member at the bottom of the opening
options.C: The beam provided across the top of the opening to carry the wall above
options.D: The projection of the slab over the opening for protection from rain

e: The jamb of a door or window opening is its vertical side, to which the frame is fixed. The bottom horizontal member is the sill and the beam across the top is the lintel.

q: The 'nosing' of a step in a staircase is:

options.A: The vertical face of the step between two successive treads
options.B: The sloping member which supports the steps of the flight
options.C: The railing provided along the open side of the staircase
options.D: The projecting front edge of the tread of the step, which extends slightly beyond the face of the riser below it

e: The nosing of a staircase step is the projecting front edge of its tread, extending slightly beyond the face of the riser below. The vertical face itself is the riser and the supporting sloping member is the stringer.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Internal check of works bills is exercised by the Accounts office before the bills are passed for payment, as a continuing departmental check.
2. Appropriation audit of works expenditure is likewise exercised by the Accounts office itself before payment of each bill.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Internal check is a continuing departmental check exercised by the Accounts office before bills are passed for payment. Appropriation audit is an audit function exercised afterwards, not by Accounts before each payment, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: In the internal check of a contractor's running bill, the quantities paid for each item, including those paid in the earlier bills of the contract, are watched against the quantities provided in the agreement primarily in order to:

options.A: Work out the total security deposit recoverable from the contractor
options.B: Detect in time any execution beyond the agreement quantities, so that the sanction for the deviation is obtained as required
options.C: Fix the rate payable for the extra items of the contract
options.D: Decide the date on which the next running bill is to be prepared

e: In internal check, cumulative quantities paid per item, including earlier bills, are watched against agreement quantities primarily to detect execution beyond agreement quantities in time, so that sanction for the deviation is obtained as required.

q: At the final settlement of a works contract, the security deposit and the performance guarantee of the contractor are released only after:

options.A: The first running bill of the next contract of the contractor has been passed
options.B: The contractor has submitted a fresh tender for another work
options.C: All recoveries and other dues of the Railways under the contract have been cleared and adjusted
options.D: The defect liability period of some other work of the same contractor has expired

e: Security deposit and performance guarantee are released at final settlement only after all recoveries and other dues of the Railways under the contract are cleared and adjusted, protecting the Railways against outstanding claims.

q: Expenditure incurred in carrying out a material modification of a sanctioned work, without obtaining the prior sanction of the competent authority for the modification, is treated as:

options.A: Ordinary repair expenditure of the division
options.B: A deposit work carried out for the contractor
options.C: Expenditure chargeable to the contingencies of the original estimate in all cases
options.D: Unsanctioned expenditure, which requires to be regularised by the competent authority

e: Expenditure on a material modification incurred without prior sanction of the competent authority is unsanctioned expenditure; it is not automatically covered by the original estimate contingencies and must be regularised by the competent authority.

q: Once a revised estimate of a work has been sanctioned, control over the expenditure on the work is thereafter exercised with reference to:

options.A: The original sanctioned estimate alone, the revised estimate being only for information
options.B: The revised sanctioned estimate, which supersedes the original estimate for purposes of control
options.C: The cost as worked out from the tender accepted for the work
options.D: The allotment made for the work in the first year of its execution

e: Once a revised estimate is sanctioned, it supersedes the original estimate for control of expenditure on the work, and further spending and deviations are watched against the revised sanctioned cost.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Once an estimate has been vetted by Finance, the responsibility for the correctness of its rates and quantities passes wholly to Finance.
2. Finance vetting of an estimate does not relieve the executive of its responsibility for the correctness of the estimate prepared by it.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Finance vetting of an estimate does not transfer responsibility for its correctness to Finance; the executive remains responsible for the correctness of the rates, quantities and other contents of the estimate it prepared, so only statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A deposit work for a private party may be taken in hand merely on the party's promise to pay the cost later, no deposit being necessary.
2. A work executed by the Railways for another Government department may be arranged on the basis of the department's acceptance of the cost, the amount being settled through adjustment in accounts.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A deposit work for a private party cannot start on a mere promise to pay; the deposit must be obtained. A work for another Government department may, however, be arranged on the department acceptance of cost, settled by accounts adjustment, so only statement 2 is correct.

q: Serviceable materials released from a work, instead of being returned to a stores depot, are taken over directly for use on another work of the Railways. In accounts, such materials are:

options.A: Treated as a free gift from the first work to the second work
options.B: Written off from the books of both the works
options.C: Charged to a suspense head permanently, without any adjustment
options.D: Credited to the work from which they were released and debited to the work on which they are used, at their assessed value

e: Serviceable released materials taken over directly for another work are credited to the work releasing them and debited to the work using them at their assessed value, so neither work gets a free benefit and accountal is complete.

q: A newly constructed railway line has been completed, opened for traffic and handed over to the open line organisation. Expenditure incurred thereafter on the assets of that line is:

options.A: Continued to be booked to the construction account of the line indefinitely
options.B: Charged to the contractor who constructed the line
options.C: Recovered from the passengers using the line as a special levy
options.D: Booked as open line expenditure under the appropriate heads, the construction account having been closed on completion and opening of the line

e: Once a new line is completed, opened for traffic and handed over to the open line organisation, its construction account is closed, and later expenditure on its assets is booked as open line expenditure under the appropriate heads.

q: An advance paid to a works contractor remains unadjusted when the contract is closed. The amount so outstanding is dealt with by:

options.A: Treating it automatically as a part of the final cost of the work
options.B: Recovering it from the final bill, the security deposit or performance guarantee, or other amounts due to the contractor
options.C: Crediting it to the revenues of the Railways as a miscellaneous receipt
options.D: Transferring it to the personal account of the Engineer-in-charge

e: An advance remaining unadjusted at closure of a contract is recovered from the contractor final bill, security deposit or performance guarantee, or other amounts due to him; it is not written into the cost of the work or treated as a receipt.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A 'New Service' is an activity or a form of expenditure of a kind not contemplated in the budget estimates of the year, which is required to be brought to the notice of Parliament.
2. A 'New Instrument of Service' is a substantial expansion of an existing service or activity, which is likewise required to be brought to the notice of Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under the GFR and budgetary procedure, a New Service is an activity or form of expenditure not contemplated in the budget estimates, and a New Instrument of Service is a substantial expansion of an existing service; both must be brought to the notice of Parliament, so both statements are correct.

q: In a lump-sum works contract, the running payments made to the contractor during the progress of the work are ordinarily made:

options.A: For the quantities of each item measured in the Measurement Book, at the schedule rates
options.B: As a percentage of the security deposit furnished by the contractor
options.C: Only after the whole work is completed and the final bill is prepared
options.D: On the completion of the stages or parts of the work laid down in the payment schedule of the contract, without item-wise measurement of quantities for payment

e: In a lump-sum contract, running payments are made on completion of the stages or parts of work laid down in the payment schedule of the contract, without item-wise measurement of quantities for payment purposes.

q: A cost-plus arrangement for the execution of a work is generally discouraged in public works mainly because, under it:

options.A: The contractor has no incentive to keep the cost of the work low, his remuneration being linked to the cost actually incurred
options.B: The measurements of the work cannot be recorded at all
options.C: No formal agreement can be executed with the contractor
options.D: The Finance branch cannot vet the estimate of the work

e: A cost-plus arrangement is discouraged because the contractor remuneration rises with the cost actually incurred, giving him no incentive to keep the cost low, which is contrary to economy in public works under the GFR principles.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In a labour contract for a work, the materials are supplied departmentally and the contractor is engaged for the labour component of the work alone.
2. Departmental materials issued to such a contractor remain his accountability until they are consumed on the work or returned, and their cost is recoverable from him if they are wasted or diverted.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: In a labour contract materials are supplied departmentally and the contractor provides labour alone; departmental materials issued to him remain his accountability until consumed on the work or returned, and their cost is recoverable if wasted or diverted, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A detailed estimate of a work is framed from its drawings and from detailed measurements of the quantities of each item of the work.
2. An abstract estimate of a work is likewise framed from detailed measurements of each and every item of the proposed work.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A detailed estimate is framed from drawings and detailed measurements of quantities of each item. An abstract estimate is framed on approximate or plinth area basis without detailed measurement of every item, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: A supplementary estimate sanctioned for a work during its execution has the effect that:

options.A: It forms a part of the original sanctioned estimate of the work, and the total cost of the work is watched against the combined sanction
options.B: It replaces the original work altogether by a new work
options.C: It can be operated upon without any allotment of funds for the work
options.D: It dispenses with the completion report of the work

e: A supplementary estimate sanctioned during execution forms part of the original sanctioned estimate, and the total cost of the work is watched against the combined sanction of the original plus supplementary estimates.

q: The net cost of a renewal or replacement work, for the purposes of its sanction and accountal, is arrived at by:

options.A: Taking the original cost of the asset when it was first created
options.B: Taking the highest cost among similar works executed on other Railways
options.C: Taking the gross cost of the new work, after giving credit for the value of the materials released from the existing asset
options.D: Ignoring altogether the materials released from the existing asset

e: The net cost of a renewal or replacement work is its gross cost minus credit for the value of materials released from the existing asset, and sanction and accountal are on this net basis.

q: In the single-packet system of tendering for a work, as distinguished from the two-packet system:

options.A: The eligibility and technical particulars and the financial offer of a tenderer are contained in a single packet and are considered together after the opening of the tenders
options.B: No financial offer is called for from the tenderers at any stage
options.C: The financial offers are opened a year after the technical offers
options.D: The tenderers are selected only by nomination

e: In the single-packet system, the eligibility and technical particulars and the financial offer are in one packet and are considered together after opening, unlike the two-packet system where the financial bids of qualified tenderers are opened later.

q: The members of a Tender Committee record differing views on a tender and the Committee is unable to make a unanimous recommendation. The tender is then decided by:

options.A: The junior-most member of the Committee
options.B: The lowest tenderer himself
options.C: Fresh voting among the tenderers
options.D: The authority competent to accept the tender, after considering the views recorded by the members of the Committee

e: Where Tender Committee members differ and no unanimous recommendation emerges, the tender is decided by the authority competent to accept it, after considering the views recorded by all the members of the committee.

q: The agreement of the Finance member of a Tender Committee to the recommendation of the Committee means that:

options.A: The estimate of the work stands sanctioned by Finance
options.B: No allotment of funds is thereafter necessary for the work
options.C: It does not by itself amount to the concurrence of Finance required for the sanction of the work, where such concurrence is separately prescribed
options.D: The accepting authority is thereafter bound to accept the tender

e: Agreement of the Finance member in a Tender Committee is to the tender recommendation only; it does not by itself amount to Finance concurrence required separately for sanction of the work where the Schedule of Powers prescribes it.

q: A firm which has prepared the Detailed Project Report and the design of a project thereafter offers to execute the same work as a contractor. Such participation is objectionable mainly because:

options.A: The firm would earn a profit on the work
options.B: It gives rise to a conflict of interest, the firm having had access to the Railways' own estimates and design basis, and the firm is ordinarily not eligible to bid for the execution of that work
options.C: The firm is not enlisted with any Railway
options.D: The work would be completed too quickly

e: A firm that prepared the Detailed Project Report and design has had access to the Railways own estimates and design basis, so its bidding for execution of the same work creates a conflict of interest and it is ordinarily not eligible to bid.

q: During execution, a contractor finds the site conditions difficult, but the conditions were such as could reasonably have been discovered by an inspection of the site before tendering. In such a case, the contractor:

options.A: Becomes entitled to a complete revision of all his rates
options.B: May abandon the work without any consequence
options.C: Cannot claim extra payment merely on the ground that he had not acquainted himself with the site conditions before submitting his tender
options.D: Is entitled to have the contract treated as a cost-plus contract

e: A contractor is deemed to have inspected and acquainted himself with site conditions before tendering; he cannot claim extra payment merely because conditions he could reasonably have discovered by such inspection turned out to be difficult.

q: Before the formal agreement with the successful tenderer for a work is executed, the draft agreement is ordinarily got vetted in order to ensure that:

options.A: The contractor obtains the maximum possible rates for the work
options.B: The tender stage can be reopened for other tenderers
options.C: The security deposit of the contractor is waived
options.D: It faithfully incorporates the Letter of Acceptance, the tender conditions and the rates accepted, without any departure from them

e: The draft agreement is vetted before execution to ensure it faithfully incorporates the Letter of Acceptance, the tender conditions and the accepted rates, without any departure from what was accepted.

q: After the tenders for a work have been opened, a clarification is sought from a tenderer about his bid. The position regarding such a clarification is that:

options.A: The tenderer may use it to quote an altogether new set of rates
options.B: It may be used to confirm or verify what is stated in the bid, but it cannot be allowed to change the substance or the price of the bid
options.C: The tenderer may withdraw his bid without forfeiting his earnest money
options.D: The clarification automatically converts the tender into a negotiated tender

e: A post-opening clarification may only confirm or verify what is already stated in the bid; it cannot change the substance or price of the bid, nor amount to a fresh quotation or a withdrawal without forfeiture.

q: In the two-packet system of tendering, the technical bids are evaluated before the financial bids are opened mainly in order to ensure that:

options.A: The technical evaluation is made without the knowledge of the prices quoted, so that it remains unbiased by the rates of the tenderers
options.B: The lowest tenderer is known before the technical scrutiny begins
options.C: The tenderers get time to revise their technical offers after seeing the rates
options.D: The Tender Committee is not required to record any recommendation

e: In the two-packet system technical bids are evaluated before financial bids are opened so that the technical evaluation is made without knowledge of the quoted prices and remains unbiased by the tenderers rates.

q: After the tenders for a work have been opened, it is proposed to alter materially the conditions on which the tenders were invited. The correct course is that:

options.A: The altered conditions may be applied to the tenders already received, with the consent of the lowest tenderer alone
options.B: The lowest tenderer may be asked to accept the altered conditions at his quoted rates
options.C: The tenders must be decided on the conditions as originally issued, or the tenders must be discharged and fresh tenders invited on the altered conditions
options.D: The Tender Committee may alter the conditions on its own authority and proceed

e: Tenders must be decided on the conditions as originally issued; if conditions are to be altered materially after opening, the tenders must be discharged and fresh tenders invited on the altered conditions.

q: Notices and orders issued to a contractor under a works contract, in order to be effective and capable of being relied upon subsequently, must ordinarily be:

options.A: Conveyed only verbally at the site of the work
options.B: Published in a newspaper
options.C: Sent only after the final bill of the contract is settled
options.D: Given in writing in the manner provided in the contract

e: Notices and orders to a contractor under a works contract must ordinarily be given in writing in the manner provided in the contract, so that they are effective and can be relied upon subsequently; verbal site instructions do not suffice.

q: A work is described in the drawings and specifications of a contract in general terms, and some minor details of its execution are not expressly described. The contractor is nevertheless bound to:

options.A: Execute the work complete in accordance with the instructions of the Engineer and sound practice, such details being treated as included in the contract
options.B: Leave out all such details and claim them as extra items in every case
options.C: Stop the work until a fresh tender is invited for the details
options.D: Execute only so much of the work as is expressly described, the rest being treated as abandoned

e: Minor details not expressly described but necessary for a complete work are treated as included in the contract; the contractor must execute the work complete per the Engineer instructions and sound practice, and cannot omit them as extras in every case.

q: An instruction of the Engineer requires a contractor to carry out work which is wholly outside the general scope of his contract. Such an instruction:

options.A: Automatically converts the contract into a new contract for that work also
options.B: Is not binding on the contractor as an instruction under the contract, unless it is issued as a variation or deviation with the sanction of the competent authority
options.C: Entitles the contractor to fix any rate he likes for the whole contract
options.D: Cancels the original contract in its entirety

e: An Engineer instruction for work wholly outside the general scope of the contract is not binding as an instruction under that contract unless issued as a variation or deviation with the sanction of the competent authority.

q: The physical and financial progress of the works sanctioned in the Works Programme is updated and monitored by the Railways through the web-based system known as:

options.A: The Indian Railways e-Procurement System used for inviting tenders
options.B: The portal used by contractors for submission of their bills
options.C: The Indian Railways Projects Sanctions and Management system
options.D: The Government e-Marketplace used for procuring common services

e: The physical and financial progress of works sanctioned in the Works Programme is updated and monitored through IRPSM - Indian Railways Projects Sanctions and Management. IREPS covers tendering and GeM covers common procurement.

q: The 'superstructure' of a bridge or a building means:

options.A: The foundation of the structure which lies below the ground
options.B: The part of the structure built over the substructure, which directly carries the loads or the traffic and is supported by the substructure
options.C: The temporary staging erected for constructing the structure
options.D: The approaches leading to the structure

e: The superstructure is the part of a bridge or building built over the substructure, which directly carries the loads or traffic and is supported by the substructure; the foundation and substructure lie below it.

q: A 'queen closer' used in brickwork is:

options.A: A brick cut in length so that its width is about half of a full brick, placed next to the quoin header to maintain the bond of the wall
options.B: A full brick laid with its length across the thickness of the wall
options.C: A brick laid at the top of a parapet wall as a coping
options.D: A defective brick which is rejected at the site

e: A queen closer is a brick cut along its length so that its width is about half of a full brick; it is placed next to the quoin header to maintain the bond of the wall at corners and junctions.

q: 'Ashlar' masonry used in the construction of a structure consists of:

options.A: Undressed stones thrown loosely into the foundation
options.B: Bricks laid without any mortar
options.C: Concrete blocks cast at the site without any reinforcement
options.D: Finely dressed stones laid in regular courses with thin and uniform mortar joints

e: Ashlar masonry consists of finely dressed stones laid in regular courses with thin and uniform mortar joints, giving a smooth finished appearance, unlike random rubble or undressed stone work.

q: 'Plastering' carried out on the walls and ceilings of a building consists of:

options.A: Filling the joints of the masonry with mortar only at the surface
options.B: Laying a floor of cement concrete over the whole room
options.C: Covering the surfaces with a coat of mortar, in order to protect the masonry and to give it a smooth and even finish
options.D: Fixing tiles over the surface of the wall

e: Plastering is covering wall and ceiling surfaces with a coat of mortar to protect the masonry and give it a smooth and even finish; merely filling joints at the surface is pointing, not plastering.

q: 'Shuttering' provided in concrete work, as distinguished from 'centering', is the formwork which is provided for:

options.A: The soffit of an arch alone
options.B: Curing the concrete after it is placed
options.C: Supporting the reinforcement bars before concreting begins
options.D: The vertical and side faces of concrete members, such as columns, beams and walls

e: Shuttering is the formwork for the vertical and side faces of concrete members such as columns, beams and walls, whereas centering is the formwork supporting soffits, such as that of an arch.

q: A 'tie' in a framed structure, such as a roof truss, is a member which is subjected mainly to:

options.A: Bending in the middle of its length
options.B: Tensile force along its length
options.C: Torsion about its own axis
options.D: Shear at its ends alone

e: A tie in a framed structure such as a roof truss is a member subjected mainly to tensile force along its length, holding the connected members together; a member mainly in compression is a strut.

q: A reinforced cement concrete slab is described as a 'one-way slab' when:

options.A: It is supported on two opposite sides and bends and spans predominantly in one direction
options.B: It is cast at the site in a single day
options.C: It contains reinforcement in neither direction
options.D: It is used only on the ground floor of a building

e: A one-way RCC slab is supported on two opposite sides and bends and spans predominantly in one direction, with main reinforcement in that direction; a slab supported on all four sides spanning both ways is a two-way slab.

q: A 'cantilever' beam or slab in a structure is one which is:

options.A: Supported at both of its ends on walls or columns
options.B: Supported at a number of points along its length
options.C: Fixed or built in at one end and free at the other end
options.D: Hung from the roof by means of steel rods

e: A cantilever beam or slab is fixed or built in at one end and free at the other end, projecting unsupported beyond its support, unlike a simply supported member resting at both ends.

q: An air-entraining admixture added to a concrete mix serves mainly to:

options.A: Remove all the water from the mix before placing
options.B: Introduce a large number of microscopic air bubbles in the concrete, which improve its workability and its resistance to frost action
options.C: Increase the weight of the concrete considerably
options.D: Prevent the reinforcement in the concrete from rusting in all cases

e: An air-entraining admixture introduces a large number of microscopic air bubbles in concrete, improving its workability and its resistance to frost action, that is, freeze and thaw damage.

q: 'Shrinkage' which takes place in concrete after it is placed in a work refers to:

options.A: The increase in the volume of the concrete as it gains strength
options.B: The settlement of the coarse aggregate to the bottom of the mix
options.C: The appearance of water on the surface of the freshly placed concrete
options.D: The reduction in the volume of the concrete as it dries and hardens, which may cause cracks if the movement is restrained

e: Shrinkage in concrete is the reduction in its volume as it dries and hardens; if this movement is restrained it may cause cracks, which is why joints and proper curing are provided.

q: A 'berm' provided in connection with a railway embankment or cutting is:

options.A: A flat ledge or strip left in the slope, or between the toe of the slope and the adjoining drain or ground, which improves the stability of the slope and helps in its drainage
options.B: A heap of surplus earth deposited at the top of the embankment
options.C: A wall of masonry built across the track
options.D: The raised portion of the formation in the middle of the track

e: A berm is a flat ledge or strip left in the slope of an embankment or cutting, or between the toe of the slope and the adjoining drain or ground, improving slope stability and helping drainage.

q: In survey and levelling work for a proposed railway work, a 'back sight' is:

options.A: The last staff reading taken before the instrument is closed for the day
options.B: A reading taken on a point whose level is not known
options.C: The first staff reading taken after the level instrument is set up, on a point of known reduced level
options.D: The difference between two successive contour lines on a plan

e: In levelling, a back sight is the first staff reading taken after the level instrument is set up, on a point of known reduced level, from which the height of instrument is worked out.

q: The 'datum' used in the levelling of a railway work is:

options.A: The highest point on the proposed alignment of the line
options.B: The reference surface or level, ordinarily the mean sea level, from which the reduced levels of points are reckoned
options.C: The first bench mark established by the contractor at the site
options.D: The level of the rail at the nearest station

e: The datum in levelling is the reference surface, ordinarily mean sea level, from which the reduced levels of all points are reckoned; bench marks are established with reference to this datum.

q: The 'contour interval' shown on a survey plan of a proposed work is:

options.A: The horizontal distance between any two contour lines on the plan
options.B: The length of the longest contour line on the plan
options.C: The number of contour lines drawn on the plan
options.D: The constant vertical distance between two successive contour lines on the plan

e: The contour interval on a survey plan is the constant vertical distance between two successive contour lines; the horizontal distance between contours is the horizontal equivalent, which varies with slope.

q: A 'joist' provided in the floor or the roof of a building is:

options.A: The main girder which carries the whole of the floor
options.B: A vertical post supporting the roof of the building
options.C: The beam provided over a door or a window opening
options.D: One of a series of closely spaced parallel beams which support the floor or the ceiling and are themselves supported on the main beams or walls

e: A joist is one of a series of closely spaced parallel beams supporting a floor or ceiling, themselves supported on the main beams or walls; it is not the main girder carrying the whole floor.

q: A project estimate prepared for a major project comprising several individual works primarily serves to:

options.A: Replace the detailed estimates of the individual works comprising the project
options.B: Record the quantities actually executed on each work of the project
options.C: Consolidate the estimated cost of all the works comprising the project, together with the other provisions of the project, so that the project as a whole can be sanctioned by the competent authority
options.D: Fix the rates at which the contracts for the works of the project will be awarded

e: A project estimate consolidates the estimated cost of all individual works comprising a major project, together with the other project provisions, so that the project as a whole can be sanctioned; it does not replace the detailed estimates of the works.

q: The 'invert level' of a culvert or a drain refers to:

options.A: The highest flood level recorded at the site of the culvert
options.B: The level of the lowest internal surface of the culvert barrel or drain at the point considered
options.C: The level of the top of the embankment over the culvert
options.D: The level of the centre line of the track above the culvert

e: The invert level of a culvert or drain is the level of the lowest internal surface of its barrel or channel at the point considered, from which its flow depth and gradient are reckoned.

q: The 'general charges' provided in the estimate of a project are intended to cover:

options.A: The cost of establishment employed on the supervision of the project and of general tools and plant, over and above the cost of the individual works
options.B: The profit payable to the contractors who will execute the works of the project
options.C: The compensation payable for the land to be acquired for the project
options.D: The interest payable on the capital borrowed for the project after its completion

e: General charges in a project estimate cover the cost of establishment employed on supervision of the project and of general tools and plant, over and above the cost of the individual works comprising the project.

q: The 'springing' of a masonry or concrete arch refers to:

options.A: The highest point of the curve of the arch
options.B: The wedge-shaped central stone of the arch
options.C: The curved intrados surface of the arch
options.D: The level or line at which the curve of the arch begins from the abutment or pier supporting it

e: The springing of an arch is the level or line at which the curve of the arch begins from the abutment or pier supporting it; the highest point of the curve is the crown.

q: A 'part estimate' sanctioned in connection with a large sanctioned work means:

options.A: An estimate prepared for only a part of the quantities of a single item of the work
options.B: A detailed estimate for a distinct portion of the work, sanctioned and taken up for execution while the detailed estimate for the remaining portion is still under preparation
options.C: An estimate for the portion of a work falling in one financial year only
options.D: An estimate for the portion of a work to be executed departmentally, as distinct from the portion given on contract

e: A part estimate is a detailed estimate for a distinct portion of a large sanctioned work, sanctioned and taken up for execution while the detailed estimate for the remaining portion is still under preparation.

q: A 'parapet' provided on a bridge or a building is:

options.A: A low protective wall provided along the edge of the bridge deck, roof or approach, to prevent persons and vehicles from falling off
options.B: A wall built below the foundation of a pier to prevent scour
options.C: A horizontal band provided on the face of a wall at the floor level
options.D: A projecting slab provided over a door or window to throw off rain water

e: A parapet is a low protective wall along the edge of a bridge deck, roof or approach, provided to prevent persons and vehicles from falling off the edge.

q: Liquidated damages levied on a contractor under a works contract in accordance with its terms can be remitted or waived:

options.A: By the Engineer-in-charge of the work on his own authority
options.B: By the contractor's representative at the site, if the delay was small
options.C: Only by the authority competent under the delegation of powers to do so, ordinarily with the concurrence of Finance and for reasons recorded
options.D: Automatically, if the contractor completes the work before the final bill is passed

e: Liquidated damages levied under a works contract can be remitted or waived only by the authority competent under the delegation of powers, ordinarily with Finance concurrence and for reasons recorded; the Engineer-in-charge cannot waive them on his own.

q: In brickwork, a 'stretcher' is a brick which is laid:

options.A: With its short end face exposed on the face of the wall
options.B: Vertically, with its length standing upright in the wall
options.C: Across the full thickness of the wall, tying its two faces together
options.D: With its long face exposed on the face of the wall, its length running along the wall

e: A stretcher in brickwork is a brick laid with its long face exposed on the face of the wall, its length running along the wall; a brick with its short end face exposed is a header.

q: A works contractor submits, after the award of the work, a detailed programme of execution in the form of a bar chart, which is approved by the Engineer. The effect of this approval is that:

options.A: The stipulated date of completion stands automatically extended to the date shown in the programme
options.B: The programme becomes the agreed sequence of the work, but its approval does not relieve the contractor of his responsibility to complete the work by the stipulated date
options.C: The Railways become responsible for any delay shown in the programme
options.D: The contractor becomes entitled to extra payment for every activity shown in the programme

e: Approval of the contractor programme or bar chart makes it the agreed sequence of work, but it does not extend the stipulated completion date nor relieve the contractor of his responsibility to complete by that date.

q: A 'strip footing' provided in the foundation of a building is:

options.A: A footing provided under an isolated column only
options.B: A raft of concrete spread under the whole area of the building
options.C: A continuous footing running along and under a load-bearing wall, spreading the load of the wall over a wider width of soil
options.D: A group of piles capped by a concrete slab under a wall
